title: The $(2,4)$-hypercontractive inequality
statement:
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function and let $\rho\in\bbr$ be a noise parameter satisfying $\rho^2\le 1/3$. Then the fourth moment of the noised function is controlled by the square of its second moment:
\[
  \E\bigl[(T_\rho f)^4\bigr]\;\le\;\bigl(\E[f^2]\bigr)^2,
\]
where $T_\rho$ is the noise operator and $\E$ denotes expectation under the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$. Equivalently, $\norm{T_\rho f}_4\le\norm{f}_2$.
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function on {0,1}^n
rho is a real noise parameter
replaced:
For any Boolean function $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ and noise parameter $\rho$ with
$\rho^2 \le 1/3$ (equivalently $\abs{\rho} \le 1/\sqrt3$),
\[
  \E[(T_\rho f)^4] \le \bigl(\E[f^2]\bigr)^2,
\]
that is $\norm{T_\rho f}_4 \le \norm{f}_2$.
